plos-pone-0003441: Stem-cell researchers found the switch that turns embryos' skin on in this 2008 paper. plos-pone-0003541: Microbiologists found bacteria bracing for trouble on a schedule in this 2008 paper. plos-pone-0003641: In 2008, a team studied how yeast cells renew their inner threads. The protein cofilin could break down actin strands even when wrapped by tropomyosin, a guard protein. The result shows cofilin works alone to turn over these guarded strands, a core trick behind cell movement.
plos-pone-0003741: In 2008, Lopes, Sucena, and Santos watched worms beat poison fast and free. plos-pone-0003841: Working in 2008, a team showed a cell-adhesion protein sweetening the cell surface. The L1 protein, acting through phospholipase C gamma, regulated the sialylation and fucosylation of surface sugars. Those sugar changes in turn tuned how nerve fibers grow, survive, and migrate.
plos-pone-0003941: In 2008, Beaufays, Adam, and Decrem catalogued a tick's spit proteins. The Ixodes ricinus tick secretes lipocalins during blood meals to blunt host defenses. The team's cloning and biochemical work maps the molecular tools of a persistent parasite.
plos-pone-0004041: In 2008, Takagaki, Lippert, and Dann fixed a calibration problem in brain imaging. They normalized voltage-sensitive dye signals against direct functional activity measures. plos-pone-0004141: In 2009, McClain, Lundsten, and Ream surveyed a deep-sea mountain thoroughly. Their seamount study mapped endemicity, biogeography, and community structure fully. The Northeast Pacific peak hosted a distinct deep community. The new census fills a blank on the ocean map.
plos-pone-0004241: In 2009, Diaz, Padler-Karavani, and Ghaderi spotted an alien sugar in people. They detected the non-human sialic acid Neu5Gc in human tissues. The dietary sugar lodged itself in our bodies. The sensitive new test maps where the foreign sugar settles.
plos-pone-0004341: In 2009, Turakainen, Saarimäki-Vire, and Sinjushina sped up slow mouse genetics. A transposition-based method generated gene-targeting vectors quite fast. plos-pone-0354141: Genome assemblies are only as good as their validation. plos-pone-0347941: Human challenge studies — deliberately infecting volunteers — promise faster vaccines but raise hard ethics. plos-pone-0358341: Postgraduates arrive with expectations — often unmet by reality. plos-pone-0356241: Dolphin milk carries microRNAs — and they look surprisingly familiar. plos-pone-0356741: Lentils feed millions — but only if yields hold steady across diverse environments. This multi-model assessment studied yield stability in lentil across multiple environments. plos-pone-0357041: How do hospital patients actually die in South Korea — and what symptoms burden their final days? plos-pone-0356141: Microwave ablation offers a less invasive fix for uterine fibroids — but measuring its effect precisely matters. plos-pone-0355941: Cannabis use disorder has no approved medications — so non-drug treatments matter enormously. plos-pone-0354341: Americans are famously confused by healthcare prices — but how confused, exactly? plos-pone-0355741: Maize landraces — farmers’ traditional varieties — harbor genetic treasures. This paper assessed phenotypic variation and diversity among them. plos-pone-0352141: Nurses who reshape their own jobs — job crafting — innovate more, but the psychology matters. plos-pone-0355841: Cancer immunotherapy research needs mice that tolerate human tumor antigens. europmc-pmc2832341: Spotting disease markers in tissue slices is routine in pathology, and this 2010 paper explains the workhorse method. europmc-pmc2877741: Rare people control HIV without drugs, and this 2010 paper hunts their secret. The authors show perforin, a killer protein, in HIV-specific CD8 T-cells tracks with elite control. europmc-pmc2913941: Joubert syndrome, a rare brain malformation seen on scans, puzzles families. This 2010 review covers Joubert syndrome and related disorders, their genes, and their care. The authors distill what is known into guidance. Their review aids diagnosis of a rare cilia disease.
europmc-pmc2939541: Frailty needs measuring in family practice before crises hit. This 2010 paper builds a frailty gauge for primary care from Europe's SHARE aging survey. europmc-pmc2940741: Ebola slips into cells by gulping itself in. This 2010 paper shows Ebola entry runs on a macropinocytosis-like gulp, then rides through early and late endosomes. The authors trace the break-in route step by step. Their work exposed targets for blocking entry.
europmc-pmc2970541: Queens and workers share genes but not fates, and this 2010 paper finds why. The authors show differential DNA methylation in the brains of queen and worker honey bees. europmc-pmc6567441: A cow's stomach is a fermentation vat, and the microbes inside decide how well she turns grass into milk. europmc-pmc6604941: Antibiotics once seemed to have won the war on germs - then the germs fought back. europmc-pmc6607541: Liver cancer hides until late - but tumor cells and DNA leaking into blood may betray it earlier.
